High-rarity classes receive equipped items with effects at their OWN recorded tiers; renamed plain travel clothes do not satisfy this rule.

rulebook-v1.0.txt.before: Item costs: COMMON 1, UNCOMMON 3, RARE 8, EPIC 20, LEGENDARY 50, UNIQUE 120. Reserve 6 points for suitable ordinary weatherwear, storage, tools and finite supplies. Four main equipment roles are class focus/weapon, protection, movement/fieldcraft, and accessory/command implement. Adapt roles to the build; a weapon is optional. Each piece uses legal slots and real weight, has immediately useful effects, and complements the actual class. Avoid four copies of one benefit or another class's entire toolkit.
rulebook-v1.0.txt.after: Item costs: COMMON 1, UNCOMMON 3, RARE 8, EPIC 20, LEGENDARY 50, UNIQUE 120. Reserve 6 points for suitable ordinary weatherwear, storage, tools, finite supplies and an ordinary weapon/focus if the class needs one. Fund four special equipment items from the remainder. The premium item means the highest-priority quality allocation, NOT a chestpiece, weapon or fixed slot.

rulebook-v1.0.txt.before: For each role in order, reserve remaining roles' floor costs BEFORE rolling. A fresh d100 of 1–20 promotes the role one tier above its base/floor if affordable after reserves; otherwise declare its promotion chance 0 before the draw. For a UNIQUE centerpiece, 1–75 gives UNIQUE and 76–100 LEGENDARY. Record every draw and allocation without rerolls. A UNIQUE class therefore receives a Legendary-or-Unique centerpiece and three Epic-or-better supporting pieces. Unused allowance expires; it is not money, a sale price, starting wealth or a future entitlement.
rulebook-v1.0.txt.after: **Precommit contextual slot weights before ANY outfit roll.** Start all sixteen legal equipment slots at weight 1 (plausible). Supply slot_preferences as a list of {slot, weight, basis} overrides: 2 for a clear fit with the actual class OR established story; 3 for both; 0 only for genuinely incompatible or player-excluded slots. Give a concrete basis for each override using actual chosen sources. Unspecified slots stay at 1. Keep at least four eligible slots and at least one justified preference above 1. Rings, Artifact, Off-Hand, Chest and every other legal slot can receive the premium allocation; no slot is reserved for it. Preserve slot spelling from the equipment schema (including Ring 1, Ring 2 and Off-Hand). Do not manipulate weights after seeing a rarity result or invent prior player history to justify them.

rulebook-v1.0.txt.before: This is a narrow once-per-creation equipment table. Ordinary loot's independent d10,000 rarity/Luck procedure, crafting and shop rules remain unchanged. Do not retroactively replace active-save equipment or erase its provenance.
rulebook-v1.0.txt.after: **Four allocations, in order:** use the premium base for the first item and the supporting floor for the other three. Before each genuine d100, reserve remaining items' floor costs. If a one-tier promotion fits after those reserves, 1–20 promotes; otherwise declare promotion chance 0 before drawing. The UNIQUE-class premium roll instead gives UNIQUE on 1–75 and LEGENDARY on 76–100. Never reroll. Thus a UNIQUE class receives one Legendary-or-Unique item in ANY eligible slot, plus three Epic-or-better items in other drawn slots.

rulebook-v1.0.txt.before: For EACH item, write name, actual rarity, equipped slot/hand requirements, weight, concrete appearance/origin, simple summary and full applicable mechanics: bonuses, triggers, targets, action/resource costs, durations and recharge. Show useful effects with short italic flavor; keep allocation arithmetic private unless requested. COMMON is competent; UNCOMMON adds focused capability; RARE supplies distinctive interactions; EPIC changes tactics; LEGENDARY grants exceptional bounded effects; UNIQUE can have singular rule-changing capability consistent with the object's function. A prestigious name or cosmetic aura alone never pays for a tier.
rulebook-v1.0.txt.after: For each allocation, select its slot by a separate genuine weighted draw: P(slot) = its committed weight / total remaining weight. Draw an integer from 1 through that total and select its cumulative ticket interval, using canonical slot order. Remove that slot before the next allocation; if only one weight-1 ticket remains, its result is certain. Weights stay fixed throughout the outfit. Record original candidates, weights/bases, slot and rarity draws, costs and unused allowance. A high-grade ring, artifact, off-hand implement, armor piece or any other plausible item can therefore receive the same premium budget. Four copies of one benefit do not make a varied kit.

rulebook-v1.0.txt.after:
For EACH item, write its name, actual rarity, drawn equipped slot/hand requirements, weight, concrete appearance/origin, simple summary and full applicable mechanics: bonuses, triggers, targets, action/resource costs, durations and recharge. Use useful class-appropriate effects with short italic flavor. COMMON is competent; UNCOMMON adds focused capability; RARE supplies distinctive interactions; EPIC changes tactics; LEGENDARY grants exceptional bounded effects; UNIQUE can have singular rule-changing capability consistent with the object's function. Points pay for functional effect grade.

**Story works in both directions.** Established class/background/story facts shape the pre-roll weights. The actual drawn equipment then informs Your story: weave in its appearance, power and plausible origin or awakening manifestation. Preserve player-authored history, beliefs and commitments. A newly manifested item can create a new narrative detail without inventing a lifelong heirloom, oath or family connection. The player may revise the generated prose.

Save four inventory records and equip them in their DRAWN slots. Save creation.outfitting with receipt action_id, allocation and item_ids in allocation order. Preserve sixteen slots, essentials and Gear-First Inventory. Unused allowance expires. This once-per-creation table leaves ordinary loot's independent d10,000 rarity/Luck, crafting and shop procedures intact. Existing receipts and active inventories remain valid; do not redraw them automatically. Outfitting adds no player-choice turn, approval or routine per-turn call.

rule-hardener.txt.before: Read 17-22/37 for advancement: freeze clocks/hazards while choices are pending; preserve tracks, offer counts, rolls and banking. Selections commit directly; when resolved, clear the freeze and continue queued actions automatically, honoring a manual pause. Chapter 19: standalone owned passives are eligible evolution sources; dependent riders are not separate skills. Save upgrades nested inside the existing base ability, preserving prior children and combined Full rules. Never add an integrated rider to Passives; further evolutions target its base skill. Read starting-gear for the once-only class-budgeted outfitting draw: four equipped, functional tier-appropriate pieces plus essentials; record receipt and item_ids. Read 23-28 for gear/weight/loot/crafting/durability, 31/32/32A for options/quests/events. Preserve the two-decision ceiling; compress routine preparation for action-seeking players without inventing attacks.
